title: Wait registration returns 201 before a background-queued commit is durable (delegation and run waits)
outcome: Found by Termal::Fable in the contract read of the run waits (mailbox #33, SHOULD 5), a pre-existing parity gap. create_delegation_wait (delegations.rs ~1083) and create_test_run_wait (test_run_waits.rs) push the wait and commit_locked, then return 201; with the background persist worker the commit is only queued, so a crash right after the response can lose a wait the agent was told is durable (the MCP tool text says 'durable'). PersistFenceTarget::WaitRegistration (persist_fence.rs) exists for exactly this but is dead code outside tests. Fix: fence both registrations (a TestRunWaitRegistration target mirroring WaitRegistration, bounded wait) before returning, or soften the tool wording. Test: background-queued persist whose fence resolves late -> the response waits for it; a failed fence -> 500 and the wait is not left half-registered.
